flows.label: Direct attachment download via tokenized URL

threats.title: Abuse — order duplication copies other teams' terms
threats.description: handleDuplicateOrder clones every field of any visible order into a new draft with no ownership check.
threats.mitigation: Restrict duplication to orders the caller created or strip cost fields.

threats.title: Denial of Service — unguarded services draft parse
threats.description: The services draft is parsed with a bare JSON.parse and no try/catch, so malformed storage blanks the app.
threats.mitigation: Wrap the services parse in try/catch with an empty-draft fallback.

threats.title: Denial of Service — fixed 4-second polling per tab
threats.description: Every open tab polls listOrders every 4 seconds with no backoff, jitter, or pause when hidden.
threats.mitigation: Add backoff, pause on hidden tabs, and prefer a change-driven subscription.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — client route guards bypassable
threats.description: RequireUser and BlockViewer decide access from React state that devtools can edit.
threats.mitigation: createOrder rejects callers whose server-resolved role is not user.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — raw server error in toast
threats.description: handleDeleteOrder surfaces the raw server error string to the end user.
threats.mitigation: Map HttpsError codes to fixed user-facing strings.

threats.title: Tampering — draft state rehydrated without validation
threats.description: Draft state is read from localStorage with no schema or range validation before entering order creation.
threats.mitigation: Validate the parsed draft against the declared types and re-validate server-side.

threats.title: Denial of Service — profile resolution blocks the UI
threats.description: setLoading(false) runs only after getMyProfile and two fallback round-trips settle, with no timeout.
threats.mitigation: Apply a client-side timeout and render with a least-privilege default.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — latent client-side rank4 promotion
threats.description: The Firestore fallback branch assigns rank4 from an email substring and is inert only because rules deny the read.
threats.mitigation: Delete the fallback branch rather than relying on rules to keep it dead.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — privilege model shipped in bundle
threats.description: The public bundle contains the department substring table and the rank4 email heuristic.
threats.mitigation: Move all role and department derivation server-side.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — role logged to console
threats.description: The resolved role is written to the browser console on every sign-in.
threats.mitigation: Remove the role from production logging.

threats.title: Spoofing — client role state editable in devtools
threats.description: Role state drives every UI decision and can be overwritten in React DevTools.
threats.mitigation: Privileged callables re-derive the role via getCallerProfile and ignore client claims.

threats.title: Tampering — optimistic department update
threats.description: updateDepartment sets local state before the callable returns and only logs failures.
threats.mitigation: Apply the state change after the callable resolves and surface failures.

threats.title: Abuse — no corporate domain restriction
threats.description: Nothing restricts sign-in to corporate email domains.
threats.mitigation: Enforce a domain allow-list in a blocking Authentication function.

threats.title: Denial of Service — targeted account lockout
threats.description: Repeated failed sign-ins against a known approver address trip Firebase throttling and lock them out.
threats.mitigation: Enable enumeration protection and monitor quota events.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — account enumeration via UI
threats.description: The UI could otherwise reveal whether an address is registered.
threats.mitigation: A single fixed message is rendered for every failure mode.

threats.title: Spoofing — no anti-automation on sign-in
threats.description: The form applies no attempt counter, lockout, backoff, or CAPTCHA.
threats.mitigation: Add App Check with reCAPTCHA Enterprise and a client-side attempt delay.

threats.title: Tampering — password rendered in plaintext in the DOM
threats.description: The visibility toggle switches the input to type=text with no time limit.
threats.mitigation: Auto-revert the toggle and reset on blur.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — client uses an unruled database
threats.description: FIREBASE_DATABASE_ID was unset so the client connected to (default), which retained permissive legacy rules while deny-all deployed to a named database; fixed and verified during this engagement.
threats.mitigation: Fixed and verified: firebase.json now uses a multi-database firestore array and deny-all rules are deployed to (default) as well as the named database.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — GEMINI_API_KEY injected into bundle
threats.description: Vite define substitutes GEMINI_API_KEY into the public bundle; the value is empty today but the pipeline is primed.
threats.mitigation: Remove the define and the unused @google/genai dependency; proxy any future Gemini call server-side.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — identity serialised into errors and logs
threats.description: handleFirestoreError serialises UID, email, tenant, and provider identities into console.error and the thrown Error.
threats.mitigation: Delete the helper and its imports or reduce it to an opaque error code.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — Firebase web config in bundle
threats.description: The Firebase web configuration is embedded in the public bundle.
threats.mitigation: Intended design — the API key is a project identifier and access is governed by Authentication plus security rules.

threats.title: Tampering — build-time config file repoints the app
threats.description: Vite silently merges firebase-applet-config.json from the project root into the compiled configuration when present.
threats.mitigation: Remove the implicit file path or require an explicit opt-in flag.

threats.title: Abuse — full scope delivered on every poll
threats.description: The list is delivered in full every 4 seconds with no pagination, enabling scripted bulk export.
threats.mitigation: Paginate listOrders server-side and rate-limit repeated full-scope requests.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — client-side admin gating
threats.description: The delete control is rendered from a client-side role test that devtools can satisfy.
threats.mitigation: deleteOrder re-resolves the role server-side and rejects non-admins.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — requester emails shown to all non-user roles
threats.description: The Created By column renders requester email addresses to viewers and every approver rank.
threats.mitigation: Render a server-resolved display name instead of the raw address.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — portfolio revenue aggregate
threats.description: Summary tiles sum totalRevenue across everything the caller can see.
threats.mitigation: Compute aggregates server-side and return them only to entitled roles.

threats.title: Abuse — orphaned attachments on failed delete
threats.description: The local reference is removed even when deleteObject rejects, leaving a reachable untracked object.
threats.mitigation: Remove the local reference only after the delete succeeds and reconcile orphans.

threats.title: Denial of Service — unbounded attachment uploads
threats.description: 100 MB uploads are permitted with no per-user quota, count limit, or cleanup of abandoned drafts.
threats.mitigation: Enforce per-user quotas and add a lifecycle rule expiring unreferenced objects.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — /manage reachable by guard bypass
threats.description: The route is gated only by the client-side RequireUser guard.
threats.mitigation: createOrder independently rejects callers whose server-resolved role is not user.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — permanent download token minted
threats.description: getDownloadURL mints a long-lived unauthenticated token that is persisted into the order document.
threats.mitigation: Store only the object path and mint short-lived signed URLs through a callable.

threats.title: Tampering — client-declared content type is the only check
threats.description: Both the client check and the storage rule validate a content type the client itself supplies.
threats.mitigation: Verify magic bytes in a Storage-triggered function and quarantine mismatches.

threats.title: Tampering — client and rules size limits disagree
threats.description: The client caps both formats at 100 MB while the rules cap PDFs at 5 MB, producing opaque failures.
threats.mitigation: Align the client limits with the rules and surface the specific rejection reason.

threats.title: Abuse — unbounded version proliferation
threats.description: Every confirmation writes a new document and no server-side cap limits versions per order number.
threats.mitigation: Cap versions per order number server-side.

threats.title: Abuse — client-supplied order number on edit
threats.description: With isNew false the server skips counter allocation and stores the client's orderNumber verbatim.
threats.mitigation: Derive orderNumber server-side from the order being amended and verify ownership.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — /report reachable by guard bypass
threats.description: The route is wrapped in a client-side BlockViewer guard that a viewer can bypass.
threats.mitigation: stripForViewer removes cost fields from viewer responses server-side.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — commission data gated client-side only
threats.description: Cost fields backing the commission panel reach every non-viewer role in the payload despite the UI gate.
threats.mitigation: Extend stripForViewer into a per-role server-side projection.

threats.title: Tampering — financial totals computed client-side
threats.description: totalRevenue, totalCost, per-service tcv and totalSST are computed in the browser and stored without recomputation.
threats.mitigation: Fixed and verified: createOrder recomputes totalRevenue, totalCost, every per-service monetary field, and the six financing metadata fields (option, totalUpfrontPayment, totalOneTimeChargeB2S, totalFinancingRequest, contractPeriod, financingLease). Confirmed across two test passes against the deployed function. See FIND-56.

threats.title: Tampering — approval depth chosen by the client
threats.description: finalDecisionAuthorityRank is derived client-side and read by approveOrder to decide where the chain terminates.
threats.mitigation: Fixed in source: createOrder recomputes each line item's Level of Authority from raw inputs and derives the order-level rank, discarding the client value.

threats.title: Tampering — client-supplied createdAt and version
threats.description: createdAt comes from the browser clock and version from a client increment, and listOrders sorts on createdAt.
threats.mitigation: Stamp createdAt with serverTimestamp and compute version server-side.

threats.title: Abuse — unlimited withdrawal from review
threats.description: The creator can withdraw after partial approvals with no limit, reason, or record.
threats.mitigation: Record withdrawals in the audit trail, cap cycles, and require a reason.

threats.title: Abuse — unbounded approval comment length
threats.description: Comments are required but never length-bounded, so approvalHistory can be inflated toward the document limit.
threats.mitigation: Enforce a maximum comment length server-side.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — approval controls rendered from client role
threats.description: Approve and reject controls are rendered from client-side role state.
threats.mitigation: Every workflow callable re-resolves role, verifies rank, department, and creator ownership server-side.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — tokenized attachment URLs rendered as links
threats.description: Stored tokenized Storage URLs are rendered directly into href attributes and retrievable with no session.
threats.mitigation: Replace the persisted URL with a callable returning a short-lived signed URL.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — commission card gated client-side only
threats.description: The commission card is hidden by a client-side role test while its input fields are delivered to every non-viewer role.
threats.mitigation: Apply a per-role server-side projection to cost fields.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — approver emails and comments shown to all viewers
threats.description: The audit log renders approver addresses and free-text comments to everyone who can see the order.
threats.mitigation: Show resolved display names and consider restricting comment visibility to the approval chain.

threats.title: Tampering — client cannot dictate workflow transition
threats.description: The component sends only orderId and comment to the workflow callables.
threats.mitigation: approveOrder and rejectOrder re-read the order and compute the transition server-side.

threats.title: Denial of Service — unguarded setItem against quota
threats.description: Both draft writes call setItem with no try/catch, so QuotaExceededError breaks the screen.
threats.mitigation: Wrap writes in try/catch, message the user, and cap draft line items.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — sensitive drafts persist after sign-out
threats.description: Cost basis, sales buffer, and customer data are stored in plaintext and never cleared on logout.
threats.mitigation: Clear draft keys on sign-out and move drafts to a server-side document.

threats.title: Repudiation — drafts carry no provenance
threats.description: Drafts have no author, timestamp, or integrity marker, so a modified draft is indistinguishable once submitted.
threats.mitigation: Persist drafts server-side with a server timestamp and owner.

threats.title: Tampering — stored draft shape unvalidated on read
threats.description: Nothing validates the shape or ranges of a stored draft when it is read back into state.
threats.mitigation: Validate the parsed draft against declared types and re-validate server-side.

threats.title: Abuse — dev server bound to all interfaces
threats.description: The dev script binds Vite to 0.0.0.0, publishing the build and its injected configuration to the local network.
threats.mitigation: Bind the dev server to 127.0.0.1 by default.

threats.title: Denial of Service — volumetric flood against the static site
threats.description: A request flood could otherwise exhaust origin capacity.
threats.mitigation: Firebase Hosting serves from Google's global CDN, which absorbs volumetric floods for static assets.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — server-side route or listing exposure
threats.description: A misconfigured rewrite could expose server-side paths or a directory listing.
threats.mitigation: A single catch-all rewrite returns index.html and the ignore list excludes dotfiles and firebase.json.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — full bundle served unauthenticated
threats.description: The rewrite serves the complete bundle, exposing route structure, role names, and callable names.
threats.mitigation: Remove privilege logic and identifying heuristics from the bundle.

threats.title: Repudiation — no deployment provenance
threats.description: Deployments are manual with no pipeline, approval gate, or record tying an artifact to a commit.
threats.mitigation: Introduce a CI/CD pipeline that builds from a tagged commit and records the deployment.

threats.title: Spoofing — site impersonation or TLS downgrade
threats.description: An attacker could otherwise impersonate the site or strip transport security.
threats.mitigation: Certificate issuance, renewal, and TLS termination are managed by Firebase Hosting.

threats.title: Tampering — no HTTP security headers
threats.description: No CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, or Referrer-Policy is set on any response.
threats.mitigation: Add a headers block setting a strict CSP, frame denial, nosniff, no-referrer, and HSTS.

threats.title: Abuse — resubmission clears approval history
threats.description: submitForApproval resets approvalHistory to an empty array, erasing earlier rank decisions.
threats.mitigation: Append a resubmission marker instead of clearing the array.

threats.title: Abuse — unlimited withdrawal stalls decisions
threats.description: withdrawFromReview may be called at any pending point with no limit and no record.
threats.mitigation: Record withdrawals, cap cycles, and require a stated reason.

threats.title: Abuse — order number grafting
threats.description: createOrder stores a client-supplied orderNumber when isNew is false without verifying ownership.
threats.mitigation: Resolve orderNumber server-side and confirm the caller created it.

threats.title: Denial of Service — unauthenticated invocation cost
threats.description: Invocations are billed before the request.auth check runs, with no rate limit, quota, or App Check.
threats.mitigation: Enable App Check, set max instances, and add per-caller rate limiting.

threats.title: Denial of Service — listOrders full-collection scan
threats.description: listOrders reads the entire orders collection on every call while the SPA polls it every four seconds per tab.
threats.mitigation: Push the role filter into the query, paginate, and replace polling with a subscription.

threats.title: Denial of Service — single hot counter document
threats.description: Order numbering serialises on one Firestore document against its per-document write ceiling.
threats.mitigation: Use a sharded counter or a distributed id scheme.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — self-provisioned rank4 role
threats.description: updateMyDepartment had no role check and wrote role rank4 with a caller-chosen department when no profile existed; fixed and verified during this engagement.
threats.mitigation: Fixed and verified: handler now requires an existing rank4 profile, validates department against an allowlist, and uses update() so profile creation is impossible.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — admin satisfies every rank
threats.description: An admin adopts whatever rank is pending, so one account can walk an order through all four stages alone.
threats.mitigation: Block a principal already present in approvalHistory and record admin overrides explicitly.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — department check fails open
threats.description: The Rank 4 department check runs only when the order carries headOfDepartment, which arrives unvalidated.
threats.mitigation: Fixed and verified: approveOrder/rejectOrder fail closed on a missing department, createOrder requires a canonical headOfDepartment, and the client approve controls match.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — client-asserted workflow state
threats.description: A client could attempt to drive a transition by submitting its own view of the order state.
threats.mitigation: Every workflow callable re-reads the order and re-resolves the caller's role server-side.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — getOrder has no authorization
threats.description: getOrder returns any order by id to any signed-in caller, stripping fields only for the viewer role.
threats.mitigation: Fixed in source: getOrder calls a canAccessOrder scope predicate mirroring listOrders and returns not-found for out-of-scope documents.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — viewer scope keyed on display name
threats.description: Viewer visibility is a case-insensitive match of accountManager against the profile name string.
threats.mitigation: Scope viewer access by a stable account identifier stored on the order.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — cost basis reaching account managers
threats.description: Cost-basis fields would otherwise reach the viewer role, which must not see internal costs.
threats.mitigation: stripForViewer removes totalCost, costPerUnit, totalSST, and salesBuffer in both getOrder and listOrders.

threats.title: Repudiation — most state changes are unaudited
threats.description: createOrder, deleteOrder, submitForApproval, withdrawFromReview, and updateMyDepartment write no audit record.
threats.mitigation: Write an append-only audit entry from every state-changing callable.

threats.title: Repudiation — hard delete leaves no tombstone
threats.description: deleteOrder permanently removes the document with no archive or record that it existed.
threats.mitigation: Replace the hard delete with a soft-delete flag plus an audit entry.

threats.title: Repudiation — approver denies having acted
threats.description: An approver could otherwise deny making a decision.
threats.mitigation: Approve and reject append entries carrying the verified token email and a server-side timestamp.

identity_key.attack_surface: no App Check enforcement on any onCall

threats.title: Spoofing — no client attestation on callables
threats.description: App Check is configured nowhere, so any HTTP client with an ID token can invoke the workflow directly.
threats.mitigation: Enable Firebase App Check and enforce it on every callable.

threats.title: Spoofing — email-keyed profile lookup
threats.description: getCallerProfile falls back to a profile document keyed by email, a weaker binding than the UID-keyed one.
threats.mitigation: Key profiles solely on UID and remove the fallback.

threats.title: Spoofing — divergent role resolvers
threats.description: getMyProfile assigns rank4 from an email substring while getCallerProfile defaults the same caller to user.
threats.mitigation: Delete the heuristic and have both resolvers share one implementation.

threats.title: Tampering — client-controlled workflow and financial fields
threats.description: createOrder wrote the client order object through, leaving status, approvalHistory, and all totals attacker-chosen; workflow fields fixed in source during this engagement.
threats.mitigation: Fixed in source: createOrder strips status, currentApprovalRank, approvalHistory, and finalDecisionAuthorityRank and sets them server-side. Stored financial totals remain client-supplied.

threats.title: Tampering — no payload schema validation
threats.description: No schema, type, range, or size validation is applied to any callable payload, and malformed fields are silently dropped.
threats.mitigation: Validate every payload against an explicit Zod schema and reject non-conforming input.

threats.title: Tampering — approval transitions are not transactional
threats.description: Read, authorization, and write happen outside a transaction, so concurrent approvals double-advance or lose entries.
threats.mitigation: Wrap the read, check, and write in runTransaction and append with arrayUnion.

identity_key.attack_surface: no backup or PITR configuration in repository

threats.title: Denial of Service — no backup or point-in-time recovery
threats.description: No backup, PITR, export, or retention configuration exists, so an erroneous bulk write or hard delete is unrecoverable.
threats.mitigation: Enable point-in-time recovery and scheduled exports, and document the restore procedure.

threats.title: Denial of Service — approvalHistory grows toward the document limit
threats.description: Audit entries accumulate in an in-document array against Firestore's 1 MiB per-document ceiling.
threats.mitigation: Move audit entries into a subcollection and bound comment length.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — direct client access to collections
threats.description: A permissive rule set would expose every order, profile, and counter to any authenticated client.
threats.mitigation: firestore.rules denies every client read and write on orders, users, counters, and the catch-all.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — no field-level encryption
threats.description: Cost, margin, commission, and customer data are stored with no field-level encryption.
threats.mitigation: Apply application-layer or KMS-backed encryption to the most sensitive fields.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — data readable from storage medium
threats.description: Data at rest could otherwise be read from the underlying storage medium.
threats.mitigation: Cloud Firestore encrypts all data at rest with Google-managed keys by default.

threats.title: Repudiation — no data-access audit logging
threats.description: Cloud Audit Logs for Firestore data access are neither enabled nor referenced, so Admin SDK reads leave no trace.
threats.mitigation: Enable Data Access audit logs and route them to a retained sink.

threats.title: Tampering — Admin SDK bypasses all security rules
threats.description: Both the functions and the migration script hold unrestricted, rules-bypassing write access to every collection.
threats.mitigation: Run each caller under a least-privilege service account scoped to the collections it needs.

threats.title: Abuse — draft prefix accumulates a permanent archive
threats.description: Objects are never moved or expired after submission, so a draft path holds an indefinite archive of quotations.
threats.mitigation: Move attachments to an order-scoped prefix on submission and apply a retention schedule.

threats.title: Abuse — bucket usable as a content distribution point
threats.description: No content scanning is applied and tokenized URLs make the bucket a trusted-domain distribution point.
threats.mitigation: Scan uploads with a Storage-triggered malware check before any download URL is issued.

threats.title: Denial of Service — no storage quota or lifecycle rule
threats.description: 100 MiB objects are permitted with no per-user quota, object count limit, or lifecycle expiry.
threats.mitigation: Enforce per-user quotas in a Storage trigger and expire unreferenced objects.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — writing into another user's prefix
threats.description: A user could otherwise write into or delete from another user's attachment prefix.
threats.mitigation: storage.rules binds both write and delete to request.auth.uid == userId.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — unauthenticated permanent download URLs
threats.description: Token-bearing URLs serve objects to anyone who presents them, with no session and no expiry, and are persisted in order documents.
threats.mitigation: Store only the object path and mint short-lived signed URLs through an authorizing callable.

identity_key.attack_surface: storage.rules:8 allow read if auth != null

threats.title: Information Disclosure — cross-user attachment reads
threats.description: The read rule grants any authenticated user access to every other user's draft attachments.
threats.mitigation: Fixed in source: storage.rules read rule scoped to request.auth.uid == userId. Closes the SDK path only — tokenized download URLs bypass rules until FIND-03 revokes them.

threats.title: Repudiation — attachment lifecycle is unrecorded
threats.description: The application records nothing about who uploaded, replaced, or removed an attachment.
threats.mitigation: Record attachment lifecycle events in the audit trail and enable Storage data-access logging.

threats.title: Spoofing — uploads attributed to another user
threats.description: Uploads could otherwise be planted under another user's identity.
threats.mitigation: The object path embeds request.auth.uid and the rule binds writes to it.

threats.title: Tampering — content type is client-declared
threats.description: The write rule validates a contentType the uploading client supplies and never inspects the stored bytes.
threats.mitigation: Verify magic bytes in a Storage-triggered function and quarantine mismatches.

identity_key.attack_surface: no blocking function restricting sign-up domain

threats.title: Abuse — no domain allow-list on accounts
threats.description: Nothing restricts which email domains may hold accounts in the project.
threats.mitigation: Add a beforeUserCreated blocking function enforcing a corporate domain allow-list.

threats.title: Denial of Service — sign-in endpoint exhaustion
threats.description: Automated sign-in attempts could otherwise exhaust the identity endpoint.
threats.mitigation: Firebase Authentication applies per-IP and per-account throttling managed by Google.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — stale privileges for token lifetime
threats.description: ID tokens stay valid for up to an hour and the app never revokes refresh tokens on role change or disablement.
threats.mitigation: Revoke refresh tokens on role change and reject tokens issued before the revocation time.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — account enumeration via identity API
threats.description: Without enumeration protection the REST endpoint distinguishes an unknown address from a wrong password.
threats.mitigation: Enable email-enumeration protection in the Firebase Authentication settings.

threats.title: Repudiation — user denies having signed in
threats.description: A user could otherwise deny having authenticated.
threats.mitigation: Sign-in successes and failures are recorded in Firebase Authentication's own logs.

threats.title: Spoofing — single-factor authentication for approvers
threats.description: Email and password is the only factor, including for CFO and CEBO approver accounts.
threats.mitigation: Enable multi-factor authentication and require enrollment for every approver role.

threats.title: Spoofing — no password policy or breach detection
threats.description: No complexity, rotation, or breached-credential policy is expressed anywhere in the repository.
threats.mitigation: Enable Identity Platform password policy and breached-credential detection.

threats.title: Tampering — forged ID token
threats.description: A forged ID token would otherwise grant arbitrary identity to the callable layer.
threats.mitigation: ID tokens are signed by Google and verified by the Functions runtime before request.auth is populated.

threats.title: Denial of Service — unbounded read and sequential writes
threats.description: The script loads every order into memory and updates documents one at a time, contending with live traffic.
threats.mitigation: Page through the collection with a cursor and apply changes in batched writes.

threats.title: Elevation of Privilege — unrestricted Admin SDK credentials
threats.description: The script initialises with ambient default credentials giving rules-bypassing write access to every collection.
threats.mitigation: Relocate the script and run it under a least-privilege service account.

threats.title: Information Disclosure — full order data pulled to a workstation
threats.description: Every order document including cost and margin fields is read into the operator's local process.
threats.mitigation: Run migrations from a controlled environment and select only the fields needed.

threats.title: Repudiation — bulk change leaves no durable record
threats.description: The script logs to stdout only and writes no record of who ran it, when, or against what.
threats.mitigation: Write a migration record into an audit collection capturing operator, timestamp, and affected ids.

threats.title: Tampering — whole services array rewritten
threats.description: The update object always includes the full services array rather than patching only the targeted field.
threats.mitigation: Patch only the specific nested fields being migrated.

threats.title: Tampering — no dry-run, backup, or idempotency guard
threats.description: The script rewrites approval-authority fields with no dry-run mode, confirmation, backup, or idempotency check.
threats.mitigation: Add a dry-run flag, require explicit confirmation, and snapshot the collection before writing.

Client connects to a Firestore database the deployed rules do not cover (resolved)
